title: Test design: Longest Run
summary: The length of the longest stretch of equal neighbours, including at the edges.
spec:
`longestRun(nums)` returns the length of the longest run of **equal adjacent values** in `nums`. For `[7, 7, 3, 3, 3, 1]` that's `3` (the three 3s).

A single value is a run of length 1. An empty array has no run: the answer is `0`.

variants.title: Doesn't count the run at the end
variants.defect: It only updates the best length when the value changes, so a longest run that reaches the end of the array is never counted.
variants.gap: In your cases, the longest run always ends before the array does. What if it's the last thing in the array?

variants.title: Says an empty array has a run of 1
variants.defect: It starts best at 1 without checking for an empty array, which has no run at all: the answer is 0.
variants.gap: The smallest possible input is worth a case of its own. What should an empty array give?

variants.title: Treats neighbours that differ by 1 as equal
variants.defect: It compares Math.abs(nums[i] - nums[i - 1]) <= 1, so 4, 5, 6 counts as one run of 3 although no two values are equal.
variants.gap: All the neighbours in your cases are either equal or far apart. Values that are close but not equal are a different class of input.

review_status: Written for practice and machine-checked: the reference and every faulty version were compiled and run with a real JDK, and each version's defect was shown on a case.
